In summary, our research is concerned with
a new type of security attack that we call hardware assisted attack.
the following question: “Can the hardware of a modern computer be used to bypass security functions provided by the operating system?”
security vulnerabilities of the hardware and their impact on the security of the software.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the security of the operating system is not sufficient to guarantee a secure system.
it is possible to circumvent the security functions of a modern operating system by exploiting undocumented hardware features.
the security of the system depends on the security of the hardware.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hardware can be used to circumvent the software.
it is possible to use undocumented processor and chipset functionalities to bypass operating system security functions and gain full control of the system.
the hardware security mechanisms are not enough to guarantee security of the whole system, especially if there are some security holes in the operating system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
security is a complex issue and that a system can be made secure only by combining different security measures.
hardware functionalities should not be considered as secure, even if they are rarely used.
the security model of an operating system is only as strong as the hardware that it runs on.
